deterministic_doctor_theorem_anchor_chec.not_a_preservation_policy: This validates already-required proof identifiers within a theorem body. It has no provider/model/tokenizer envelope, PCSM source-map or slice binding, natural-anchor candidate input, cost or semantic-utility decision, deterministic ranking, alias collision control, alias-table output, or preservation receipt. It cannot be repurposed as PCSM minification authority.

pcsm_042_token_cost_prerequisite.determinism_and_binding: It provides immutable content-addressed provider/model/tokenizer envelopes and deterministic calibrated-fallback accounting. Provider-native usage is measured only when supplied; calibrated fallback is explicitly estimated.
pcsm_042_token_cost_prerequisite.not_a_preservation_policy: Token accounting has no natural-anchor candidate input or selection outcome. Token cost alone cannot determine whether requests.get, pytest.fixture, asyncio.Lock, DuckDB, CID, Quack, Lean, or Z3 remains readable or semantically useful.

limitations: This receipt is a current-head capability assessment and non-promotion disposition, not a semantic-anchor preservation policy, alias table, source linker, semantic proof, or promotion decision.
DoctorReviewedTheorem checks anchors in a proof body only; it cannot decide whether an alias should be preserved in a semantic-minified projection.
PCSM-042 token accounting is a reusable prerequisite only. A measured or calibrated token count alone never establishes semantic utility, readability, safe retention, or an alias decision.
Missing plan dimensions are not reported as zero, passing, or fulfilled by adjacent controls.
Only the declared receipt changed. The task's exact edit authority excludes the missing product implementation and test paths.
This receipt has no immutable self-CID because minting a self-describing CID would change its bytes.
